hook.line: Official Spanish loves nouns. Where a friend says "after we signed", a notice on the door says "after the signing". Learn the trick and legal and administrative texts stop looking like a wall.
hook.es: Tras la firma del contrato, se anunció el cierre del local.
hook.en: After the contract was signed, the closure of the premises was announced.

rule:
Spanish can turn an action into a thing. *Firmar* (to sign) becomes *la firma* (the signing); *cerrar* becomes *el cierre*; *llegar* becomes *la llegada*; *vender* becomes *la venta*; *abrir* becomes *la apertura*.

Who or what the action belongs to follows with *de*: *la llegada de Yesid*, *la venta del edificio*. The English "Yesid's arrival" turns around.

This lets you squeeze a whole clause into a short opener. Instead of "After the contract was signed", write *Tras la firma del contrato*. Instead of "When Yesid arrived", write *Con la llegada de Yesid*.

Every one of these is a real noun with its own gender: *la* firma, *el* cierre. Learn each with its little word, because the ending does not always tell you.
smallPrint: Teachers call this nominalisation: making a noun from a verb. The nouns are often called deverbal nouns.

readAndPick.es: Tras la firma del contrato, Tomás habló con Vale.
options: After the contract was signed, Tomás spoke with Vale.
Before the contract was signed, Tomás spoke with Vale.
Because of the contract, Tomás spoke with Vale.

readAndPick.es: La llegada de Yesid cambió todo.
options: Yesid's departure changed everything.
Yesid's arrival changed everything.
Yesid changed everything.

readAndPick.es: La venta del edificio preocupa a Don Hernando.
options: The purchase of the building worries Don Hernando.
The building worries Don Hernando.
The sale of the building worries Don Hernando.

readAndPick.es: La compra del edificio es imposible.
options: The purchase of the building is impossible.
The sale of the building is impossible.
The building is impossible.

readAndPick.es: Antes de la reunión, hablé con Vale.
options: After the meeting, I spoke with Vale.
During the meeting, I spoke with Vale.
Before the meeting, I spoke with Vale.

readAndPick.es: El cierre del café fue una sorpresa.
options: The closure of the café was a surprise.
The opening of the café was a surprise.
The café was a surprise.

readAndPick.es: La entrega de los documentos es el lunes.
options: The documents are delivered on Monday.
The delivery of the documents is on Monday.
The delivery of the document is on Monday.

options: With the arrival of Altamira, the neighbourhood changed.

When Altamira arrives, the neighbourhood changes.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *llegada* or *llegar* and type the sentence: *La ___ de Yesid cambió todo.*
yourTurn.answer: La llegada de Yesid cambió todo.
yourTurn.why: After *la* you need the noun, *llegada*, not the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *cierre* or *cerrar* and type the sentence: *El ___ del café fue una sorpresa.*
yourTurn.answer: El cierre del café fue una sorpresa.
yourTurn.why: *Cierre* is the noun for "the closing", and it is masculine.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The sale of the building worries Don Hernando.
yourTurn.answer: La venta del edificio preocupa a Don Hernando.
yourTurn.why: *De* + *el* joins into *del*, and *a* comes before a person.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The opening of the café is at eight.
yourTurn.answer: La apertura del café es a las ocho.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it with a noun after *Tras*: *Después de firmar el contrato, Tomás habló con Vale.* Say: After the contract was signed, Tomás spoke with Vale.
yourTurn.answer: Tras la firma del contrato, Tomás habló con Vale.
accept: Después de la firma del contrato, Tomás habló con Vale.
yourTurn.why: *Firmar* becomes *la firma*, and *del contrato* says what was signed.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it with a noun after *Con*: *Cuando llegó Yesid, todos se alegraron.* Say: With the arrival of Yesid, everyone was glad.
yourTurn.answer: Con la llegada de Yesid, todos se alegraron.
yourTurn.why: *Cuando llegó Yesid* shrinks to *con la llegada de Yesid*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The delivery of the documents is on Monday.
yourTurn.answer: La entrega de los documentos es el lunes.
yourTurn.why: *Entrega* is the noun, and *de los documentos* says what is delivered.

pitfalls.wrong: La firmar del contrato es mañana.
pitfalls.right: La firma del contrato es mañana.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *la* you need the noun *firma*, not the verb *firmar*.

pitfalls.wrong: El llegada de Yesid cambió todo.
pitfalls.right: La llegada de Yesid cambió todo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Llegada* is feminine, so it takes *la*.

pitfalls.wrong: La venta el edificio preocupa a Don Hernando.
pitfalls.right: La venta del edificio preocupa a Don Hernando.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The owner follows with *de*, and *de* + *el* becomes *del*.

pitfalls.right: La llegada de Yesid cambió todo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. In Spanish the noun comes first and the owner follows with *de*; there is no "Yesid's" shortcut.

personal: Write one sentence about your own town or job that starts with a noun made from a verb, such as *La apertura de…* or *La llegada de…*.
